messages:
Priya: noticed unusual pattern in audit logs: several DB snapshot uploads and object PUTs with missing kms key id. looks like snapshots-landfill prefix affected.
Marcus: can you paste the CloudTrail sample?
Priya: pasted: 
```
EventName: PutObject
User: arn:aws:sts::111111:assumed-role/svc-snap-uploader
Bucket: snapshots-archive
Key: tenant77/db-snap-2026-03-17.rdb.gz
additionalEventData: { \"x-amz-server-side-encryption\": \"AES256\" }
```
Alex: that 1) confirms SSE-S3 not SSE-KMS, 2) check KMS grants for svc-snap-uploader role and any recent role/iam changes.
encops-bot: alert ENCOPS: S3 non-KMS write detected for snapshots-archive (rule ENC-DR-009). Suggested runbook: /runbooks/encryptops/s3-non-kms-detect.
Marcus: pulled terraform history: change 2026-03-16 removed kms:Encrypt on role svc-snap-uploader when converting to org-managed keys. Change owner: infra-automation.
Priya: are there database snapshot uploads too or only object-store? This could be the backup pipeline writing DB exports with SSE-S3.
Alex: checked RDS export logs: export-to-s3 call used by rds-exporter has parameter Sse=AES256 in 3 runs at 03:14-03:19 UTC. Looks correlated.
Marcus: immediate containment ideas: 1) update bucket policy to DENY PutObject unless x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id present, 2) push an IAM inline deny on svc-snap-uploader, 3) roll back terraform change. Which is least risky?
Priya: bucket policy deny is safer (scoped to bucket) and prevents other principals from bypassing. But must ensure there aren't other legitimate processes that expect SSE-S3.
ops-oncall: can implement bucket policy now, ETA 5m. I'll add explicit deny with condition sse != aws:kms and allow list for service account pool during hunting window.
Alex: while we block, we need forensics: list all keys in snapshots-archive without x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id and capture object size, owner tag, and last-modified. We'll also run a DB-restore-sim check to ensure these unencrypted snapshots are not used in internal restores.
Marcus: I've kicked a lambda scanner to enumerate objects and wrote results to s3://ops-temp/encops/1865439999-unencrypted.csv.
Priya: vuln triage: severity P2 (confidentiality), notify legal/compliance + customers if scope includes customer data. Tag incident ENC-2026-03-17-01.
encops-bot: generated incident checklist: notify stakeholders, preserve logs, implement mitigation, re-encrypt objects, perform postmortem.
Alex: re-encryption strategy: server-side copy to same key with --metadata-directive REPLACE and --server-side-encryption aws:kms. For large DB snapshots (>10GB) prefer s3api copy-object to avoid transfer. Example: 
```bash
aws s3api copy-object --bucket snapshots-archive --copy-source snapshots-archive/tenant77/db-snap-2026-03-17.rdb.gz \
  --key tenant77/db-snap-2026-03-17.rdb.gz --server-side-encryption aws:kms --ssekms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111:key/abcd
```
Marcus: caution: copy-object requires kms:Encrypt on caller. Since we removed kms perms, need to temporarily grant a scoped KMS grant or restore role permission. Consider creating an ephemeral KMS grant to the service account principal with TTL 1 hour using CreateGrant + retiring policy.
Priya: agree. Forensics-first: create separate service account svc-reencrypt with minimal s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, kms:Encrypt on that key only and run re-encrypt job from ephemeral container. That limits blast radius.
ops-oncall: provisioning svc-reencrypt now.
Alex: add monitoring: SIEM rule to surface PutObject where additionalEventData.x-amz-server-side-encryption != aws:kms and also where kmsKeyId not present. Attach severity high.
Marcus: RBAC change control: update Terraform PR template to require reviewers to check KMS policy diffs; add automated lint that flags removal of kms:Encrypt on principals used by backup/snapshot services.
Priya: also update our CI smoke test for backup flows: when infra PRs touch iam roles used by backup agents, run a simulated upload to a test bucket and assert SSE-KMS present.
encops-bot: logged compliance notification: legal@redwood.example, compliance@redwood.example.
Alex: outcome summary so far: bucket policy applied to deny non-KMS uploads, scanner enumerating affected objects, ephemeral reencrypt role being provisioned, detection rule created, legal notified. Next: confirm tenant list and decide on customer notification if any tenant snapshots contained PII.
Priya: I'll correlate object prefixes with tenant metadata and produce list for incident report. Will attach to incident ticket.
Marcus: schedule postmortem RFC for next week to go through root cause and process changes.
ops-oncall: rolling patch applied, monitoring for errors in backup pipeline.
Priya: thanks everyone, keep updates concise here. We'll escalate if restores are attempted.
summary: Detected DB snapshot and object uploads to snapshots-archive using SSE-S3 (AES256) after an IAM change removed kms:Encrypt. Team applied bucket-level deny, enumerated affected objects, provisioned a scoped re-encrypt role, created SIEM detection, and opened an incident for compliance review.
